description: We're CosmicCanvas, building an interactive tool using NASA Earth data to help farmers adapt to climate change. Our platform maps temperature, rainfall and soil moisture trends, then provides practical crop and planting advice with a “What If?” climate slider and local-language support. We’re looking for developers, data analysts, designers and storytellers.
summary: CosmicCanvas is a free, map-based decision-support tool that helps farmers choose crop rotations that protect soil and save water. A farmer draws a field and sets priorities such as water savings, soil health, income or erosion control. The tool combines NASA Earth observations (SMAP soil moisture, GPM IMERG rainfall, Landsat/MODIS NDVI, ECOSTRESS heat and evapotranspiration, SRTM terrain, NASA POWER climate) with local soil, crop and price data. It then compares three rotation strategies: the current rotation, a cover-crop rotation, and a legume/drought-tolerant rotation. Each strategy gets plain-language scores, risks and confidence ranges. Scenario sliders show how each option holds up under changing rainfall and temperature. CosmicCanvas supports farmer judgment and does not replace it.
details:
What it does: The farmer draws a field and sets priorities and constraints. CosmicCanvas pulls about 10 years of data, resamples it to a common 30 m grid and monthly time step, and builds four 0-100 scores: water stress, heat stress, erosion risk and soil-health trend. It then scores three rotation strategies with a weighted model that uses the farmer’s priorities. The model also accounts for nitrogen fixing, cover duration, root depth and water demand. The output is a ranked comparison with reasons, key risks and “check with a local expert” flags.

Benefits and impact: Farmers get a simple, local, data-based way to compare rotations. The tool helps them conserve water, reduce erosion and rebuild soil. It can scale to any region with data coverage.

Interface: An interactive map with soil moisture, NDVI and erosion layers and a timeline slider. Rainfall and temperature sliders test each strategy. Result cards use large text, plain language and icons for low technical experience.

Uncertainty: Satellite data differs from ground measurements, so every score shows a confidence range. The tool shows patterns and possibilities and does not give guarantees.

Tools: Python, xarray, rasterio, scikit-learn, Earthdata APIs, React, Leaflet.

Creativity: It fuses several NASA datasets into one farmer-priority score and keeps the farmer in control.
